subject: Vocabulary
topic: Phobia and Mania — Fear Words and Compulsion Words for SSC CGL One-Word Substitution (W13 B1)

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an abnormal fear of enclosed spaces'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CLAUSTROPHOBIA = fear of enclosed or confined spaces (Latin: claustrum = enclosed place + phobos = fear). People with claustrophobia fear lifts, small rooms, tunnels. Trap: AGORAPHOBIA = fear of open or crowded public spaces (the opposite — open, not enclosed); XENOPHOBIA = fear/hatred of foreigners; ACROPHOBIA = fear of heights.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an abnormal compulsion to steal'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. KLEPTOMANIA = an irresistible urge to steal, often without need or desire for the stolen item (Greek: kleptes = thief + mania = obsession). A kleptomaniac steals compulsively, not for profit. Trap: DIPSOMANIA = compulsive excessive drinking/alcoholism; PYROMANIA = compulsive urge to set fires; MEGALOMANIA = obsessive preoccupation with one's own power or importance.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an intense fear or dislike of foreigners or people from other countries'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. XENOPHOBIA = an intense or irrational fear or dislike of people from other countries; hostility towards foreigners (Greek: xenos = stranger/foreigner + phobos = fear). It is often used in a social/political context to describe prejudice against immigrants. Trap: MISANTHROPY = hatred of humankind in general (not specifically foreigners); AGORAPHOBIA = fear of open or public spaces; CYNOPHOBIA = fear of dogs.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an obsessive enthusiasm for collecting and possessing books'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. BIBLIOMANIA = an obsessive preoccupation with collecting and possessing books (Greek: biblion = book + mania = obsession). A bibliomaniac collects books compulsively, sometimes beyond any hope of reading them all. Trap: GRAPHOMANIA = compulsive urge to write; LOGOMANIA = compulsive use of words/talking; MONOMANIA = obsession focused on a single idea or subject (books would fall under monomania, but bibliomaniac is more specific).

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'a person with a morbid compulsion to set fire to things'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. PYROMANIAC = a person who has a compulsive desire to set fire to things (Greek: pyr = fire + mania = obsession). This is distinct from ARSONIST (who sets fires for gain or revenge); a pyromaniac sets fires compulsively for the satisfaction of the act. Trap: KLEPTOMANIAC = compulsive stealer; DIPSOMANIAC = compulsive drinker; note also: ACROPHOBIA (fear of heights) vs PYROPHOBIA (fear of fire) — the SSC often tests fear of fire vs compulsion to set fire.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an abnormal fear of water'?
questions.explanation: B is correct. HYDROPHOBIA = fear of water (Greek: hydor = water + phobos = fear). It is also the medical term for a symptom of rabies, where sufferers experience fear and inability to swallow water. Trap: THALASSOPHOBIA = fear of the SEA or large bodies of water specifically (not water in general — more specific than hydrophobia); BATHOPHOBIA = fear of depth; CRYOPHOBIA = fear of cold. 'Hydrophobia' is the classic SSC answer for 'fear of water'.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an obsession with one's own power and importance; a delusional belief that one is greater than one is'?
questions.explanation: D is correct. MEGALOMANIA = obsession with one's own power; a delusional mental state in which a person believes they are much greater, more powerful or more important than they actually are (Greek: megas = great + mania = obsession). 'A megalomaniac dictator believed himself to be the saviour of the world.' Trap: NARCISSISM = excessive self-love and vanity (related but focused on physical appearance and admiration); MONOMANIA = obsessive preoccupation with a SINGLE idea (can be any fixation, not specifically power); ERGOMANIA = compulsion to work excessively.

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'an abnormal fear of being in open or crowded spaces, especially in situations where escape might be difficult'?
questions.explanation: C is correct. AGORAPHOBIA = fear of open or public spaces, especially situations where it might be difficult to escape (Greek: agora = marketplace/open space + phobos = fear). Agoraphobics often avoid shopping malls, public transport and open plazas. Trap: CLAUSTROPHOBIA = the opposite: fear of ENCLOSED spaces; ACROPHOBIA = fear of HEIGHTS (not crowds/open spaces); DEMOPHOBIA = fear of crowds specifically (demophobia is a term sometimes used, but agoraphobia is the broader, more standard term that includes crowded public spaces and is SSC's standard answer).

questions.stem: What is the one-word substitution for 'a compulsive or obsessive preoccupation with gambling'?
questions.explanation: D is correct. LUDOMANIA = a compulsive urge to gamble; pathological gambling disorder (Latin: ludus = game + mania = obsession). Also sometimes called 'gambling disorder'. Trap: DROMOMANIA = compulsive urge to travel/wander; DIPSOMANIA = compulsive drinking; TYCHOMANIA = while used in some vocabulary lists, 'ludomania' is the more precise and commonly tested term for gambling compulsion. SSC one-word substitution questions increasingly test these Latin-derived '-mania' words.

questions.stem: Match correctly: Which pair is INCORRECT? (Phobia = fear of...)
questions.explanation: D is correct — D is the INCORRECT pair. ARACHNOPHOBIA = fear of SPIDERS (and arachnids, not reptiles). Greek: arachne = spider (from the myth of Arachne, transformed into a spider by Athena). The fear of reptiles is HERPETOPHOBIA (from Greek herpeton = reptile). Verify the correct pairs: ACROPHOBIA = heights (Greek: akros = highest point) ✓; CYNOPHOBIA = dogs (Greek: kyon = dog) ✓; ORNITHOPHOBIA = birds (Greek: ornithos = bird) ✓. Only ARACHNOPHOBIA = reptiles is WRONG (spiders ≠ reptiles).
